MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 16, 2019

  The Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:00
  p.m. at City Council Chambers 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California
  by CHAIR RETZ.

  1.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Retz, Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla & Bain

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Romanelli & McCormick

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Comm. Services Coordinator

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 19, 2019

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 19, 2019

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  JOINT MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 20, 2019

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 20, 2019 AS AMENDED

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 16, 2019
   6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  VETERAN’S MEMORIAL DONATION

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if irrigation and maintenance costs if any, would be covered by the
  donor.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted that maintenance staff will work with Bennett
  Landscape to create a drip system to provide irrigation of memorial plants.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if this project could also be done as an Eagle Scout project
  to possibly offset cost.

  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO stated that the project required cementing which would
  best be handled by a professional and that an Eagle Scout project could be added
  alongside the memorial.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted a bench was part of the proposal which could
  be a possible Eagle Scouts project and staff will explore that option.

  CHAIR RETZ noted a possible drainage issue from the concrete work could damage
  plants and cause further maintenance issues and that the project should be tabled until
  the issue is clarified.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted the lighting around the base of the flag pole be
  stretched out to meet the footprint of the new memorial so that the flag could still be lit
  from the ground.

  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that maintenance staff will move the lighting to
  accommodate the memorial.

  CHAIR RETZ inquired about the long term maintenance cost to the memorial.

  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that final maintenance costs have not been
  confirmed.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted that the landscaping contract with Bennett
  Landscape covers the area of the memorial along with the City Hall service and that staff
  will inquire about a more detailed and itemized list of services by Bennett Landscape to
  better analyze the long term cost of maintenance of the memorial.

  CHAIR RETZ wanted to know the annual cost of maintenance for the memorial so that it
  could be approved by the Commission.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the donor underwrote annual maintenance costs when
  requesting to build the memorial and if they could approve any possible annual

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 16, 2019
   maintenance costs associated with the memorial and that it be clear to the donor what the
  total costs include.

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, to:

  TABLE THE VETERAN’S MEMORIAL DONATION UPON FINALIZING
  DRAINAGE AND MAINTENANCE COSTS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA provided an overview per agenda
  material.

  CHAIR RETZ observed that the fee increase did not match the verbal report given by
  COORDINATOR AHAJA.

  COMMISSIONER POPE clarified the calculated parade fees and noted that the fee
  increase was only $250.00.

  COORDINATOR AHAJA clarified further that the secondary budget is in name only and
  that it covers the judging of the parade.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for further clarification about the fees; which was explained
  by COMMISSIONER POPE to include Parade Coordination of $9,750, which is $250
  above the fee from last year, and a Secondary budget item for judging of $1,500 for a total
  cost of $11,250.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA
  to:

  TO MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO ENTER INTO THE
  ATTACHED AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY PARADES TO PROVIDE
  PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY
  PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 7, 2019.

  CHAIR RETZ REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  Ayes: Bain, Ciarolla, Persichina, Retz, Pope
  Noes: None
  Absent: McCormick, Romanelli

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 16, 2019
   7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted a horse got out of their stall and was hit on
  Hawthorne Blvd. on Friday 9/6/2019 and was wondering how to keep horses from leaving
  Ernie Howlett Park. He suggested having the Equestrian Committee look into the matter.

  B.  PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that there were no issues to bring up and that the
  parade Marshalls will be announced during the next meeting.

  C.  HILLS ARE ALIVE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that a spot before the Botanic Garden was a
  small problem this year and that the number of participants have declined again this
  year.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS OFSEPTEMBER 10, 2019

  Received and filed.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  SPECIAL EVENT PERMITS

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that the current policies
  in place do not cover special events specifically and that staff is working on a process to
  help organize such events.

  B.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION LOGO

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS stated that a revised logo will be available in
  October along with alternative logos.

  C.  SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO stated that more information
  from Little League may come to the Commission on a possible transition to Pony Colt
  League, but as of now they will continue as Little League Baseball.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 16, 2019
   11.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted volunteers are still
  needed for the Pepper Tree Booth during the City Celebration. COMMISSIONER BAIN
  agreed to volunteer for the morning shift.

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:34 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON OCTOBER 22, 2019 AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET AT
  CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Services Coordinator  Community Services Supervisor

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 16, 2019
